119:     public static void serverTick(Level level, BlockPos pos, BlockState state, AlchemyFurnaceBlockEntity furnace) {
120:         if (level.isClientSide()) {
121:             return;
122:         }
123:         WorldStateData data = CharacterStore.data(level.getServer());
124:         long now = data.worldActiveMillis();
125:         if (furnace.lastSettledWorldMillis <= 0L) {
126:             furnace.lastSettledWorldMillis = now;
127:             tickOnce(furnace);
128:             return;
129:         }
130:         long delta = now - furnace.lastSettledWorldMillis;
131:         if (delta >= 50L) {
132:             int ticks = (int) Math.min(36_000L, delta / 50L);
133:             int beforeOutput = furnace.items.get(SLOT_OUTPUT).getCount();
134:             boolean changed = false;
135:             for (int i = 0; i < ticks; i++) {
136:                 if (!tickOnce(furnace)) {
137:                     break;
138:                 }
139:                 changed = true;
140:             }
141:             furnace.lastSettledWorldMillis = now;
142:             if (delta >= 1_000L) {
143:                 furnace.lastCatchupSeconds = (int) (delta / 1000L);
144:                 furnace.lastCatchupItems = Math.max(0, furnace.items.get(SLOT_OUTPUT).getCount() - beforeOutput);
145:                 changed = true;
146:             }
147:             if (changed) {
148:                 furnace.setChanged();
149:             }
150:             return;
151:         }
152:         furnace.lastSettledWorldMillis = now;
153:         tickOnce(furnace);
154:     }

156:     private static boolean tickOnce(AlchemyFurnaceBlockEntity furnace) {
157:         AlchemyRecipes.Recipe recipe = AlchemyRecipes.find(furnace.items.get(SLOT_FIRST), furnace.items.get(SLOT_SECOND));
158:         boolean changed = false;
159:         int currentMax = furnace.maxProgress();
160:         int newStatus;
161:         if (recipe == null) {
162:             newStatus = 0;
163:         } else if (!AlchemyRecipes.isFuel(furnace.items.get(SLOT_FUEL)) && furnace.progress == 0) {
164:             newStatus = 1;
165:         } else if (!canOutput(furnace.items.get(SLOT_OUTPUT), recipe)) {
166:             newStatus = 2;
167:         } else if (furnace.progress > 0) {
168:             newStatus = 3;
169:         } else {
170:             newStatus = 4;
171:         }
172:         if (newStatus != furnace.status) {
173:             furnace.status = newStatus;
174:             changed = true;
175:         }
176:         if (recipe == null || !canOutput(furnace.items.get(SLOT_OUTPUT), recipe)) {
177:             if (furnace.progress != 0) {
178:                 furnace.progress = 0;
179:                 changed = true;
180:             }
181:         } else if (furnace.progress == 0) {
182:             if (AlchemyRecipes.isFuel(furnace.items.get(SLOT_FUEL))) {
183:                 furnace.items.get(SLOT_FUEL).shrink(1);
184:                 furnace.progress = 1;
185:                 changed = true;
186:             }
187:         } else {
188:             furnace.progress++;
189:             changed = true;
190:             if (furnace.progress >= currentMax) {
191:                 finishRecipe(furnace, recipe);
192:                 furnace.progress = 0;
193:                 changed = true;
194:             }
195:         }
196:         if (changed) {
197:             furnace.setChanged();
198:         }
199:         return changed;
200:     }

202:     private static boolean canOutput(ItemStack output, AlchemyRecipes.Recipe recipe) {
203:         if (output.isEmpty()) {
204:             return true;
205:         }
206:         if (!output.is(recipe.output())) {
207:             return false;
208:         }
209:         return output.getCount() < output.getMaxStackSize();
210:     }

Let me read loot table to see if it drops items (not container). That matters: breaking furnace with a pickaxe triggers onRemove -> dropContents. But loot table drops only the block itself; contents dropped separately. However, is there double drop? only block. Fine.

Also check BaseContainerBlockEntity stillValid behavior for distance. And check whether onRemove with block replace by same block? `state.is(newState.getBlock())` handles.

Potential bugs to reason:

1. ejectInputs loops SLOT_FIRST, SLOT_SECOND, SLOT_OUTPUT. It clears slots then attempts player inventory add, drop if fail. Inventory.add mutates copy but if partial insertion, `add` returns false and may have partially inserted? In Minecraft, `Inventory.add(ItemStack)` loops and adds to matching stacks / empty slots; it returns true if stack becomes empty. Important: it mutates the passed stack (copy). If partially added, remainder is on copy and gets dropped. That's correct, no loss. So no dupe.

But note: while iterating, if player inventory is the same as furnace? No.

2. Progress reset: sets progress=0, but does not reset `status`. Status stays stale e.g. 3 (running) until next tick. tickOnce next tick recomputes: recipe null -> status 0. Since items empty, next tick resets status. So transient status residue one tick, but client menu data sync? The menu data is server ContainerData; client reads synchronized values. After eject, status remains e.g. 3 until next server tick updates and AbstractContainerMenu broadcasts? Actually data slots sync via ServerboundContainer... The server sends changes when detectAndSendChanges (broadcastChanges) each tick. So residual status may show for one tick (50ms). Is that "工序状态残留"? progress is reset, status not. Also lastCatchup values not reset — those display "离线追赶" message may persist. Minor.

3. More significant: ejectInputs does not reset `progress` if nothing in furnace (returns false before progress=0). But if no items, can progress be > 0? Yes! tickOnce: when progress>0, recipe non-null and canOutput true, progresses. If recipe exists in slots, progress>0 means items exist. Could progress>0 with empty input slots? progress only increments when recipe found, and resets to 0 when recipe null. So no. However, consider a slot with count below recipe count? recipe null -> progress reset. So progress>0 implies inputs nonempty, also fuel. But then "any" true. Unless... items emptied externally without tick? e.g., hopper extraction? Does the BE expose items to hoppers? BaseContainerBlockEntity implements Container; NeoForge capability for item handler? Without capability registration, hoppers may use Container via vanilla? In NeoForge, vanilla hopper uses Capabilities.ItemHandler, which is automatically wrapped for Container BEs? NeoForge provides `CapabilityItemHandler` via `Inventory`? Actually NeoForge auto-wraps `Container` with `InvWrapper` if `ICapabilityProvider`... BlockEntity doesn't automatically expose. NeoForge's `CapabilityHooks`? Uncertain — write unverified.

4. Critical: ejectInputs can be called via clickMenuButton while furnace tick also runs. Both on server thread, no concurrency. fine.

5. Output slot: output is in container and menu slot with mayPlace false, but player can still TAKE from it (correct). quickMoveStack handles. ejectInputs also includes output. Fine.

But crucial: `canOutput` checks output stack max size; finishRecipe does `output.grow(produced.getCount())` when same item. canOutput ensures count < maxStackSize, but doesn't ensure count + produced.getCount() <= maxStackSize. So output can exceed max stack size (e.g., 64 + 2 = 66). Is that a dupe/loss? It's overstack, not loss. However further: if output count reaches maxStackSize exactly or beyond, canOutput false -> progress reset to 0, stopping. No item loss (items already in output). Overstack stacks could be problematic when taking—can take? player can pick up full stack 66. Not loss. But is this "吞物品"? Not exactly. Yet there is a real item loss scenario: `finishRecipe` is called after consuming inputs: first.shrink, second.shrink, then if output not empty and different item... but canOutput ensured output empty or same item. Wait canOutput checked at tick start; no change between? finishRecipe happens within same tick iteration, output unchanged since check. So safe.

But: `first.shrink(recipe.firstCount())` uses the recipe matched order. Recipe.find checks recipe.matches(first, second) || matches(second, first). If matched reversed (slot0 has second ingredient, slot1 first), then `finishRecipe(furnace, recipe)` uses recipe.firstCount on slot0 and recipe.secondCount on slot1 — wrong counts! Example recipe: SPIRIT_DEW_HERB(2) + GREEN_VEIN_HERB(1) -> QI_GATHERING_POWDER. Put first slot GREEN_VEIN x1, second slot SPIRIT_DEW x2. matches(second, first)? find calls recipe.matches(first,second) where first=slot0 GREEN. recipe.matches requires slotFirst.is(SPIRIT_DEW) false. Then recipe.matches(second, first) -> checks slot0? matches(arg1=slot1 SPIRIT, arg2=slot0 GREEN) -> true. Then finishRecipe shrinks slot0 by recipe.firstCount=2 (GREEN 1 -> shrink 2 => empty, consumes whole stack of 1 but recipe requires 1; only loses 1), and slot1 by recipe.secondCount=1 (SPIRIT 2->1), leaving 1 SPIRIT unused but consumed? Actually consumes 1 SPIRIT instead of 2 → extra SPIRIT retained. Hmm item loss? slot0 green count 1 shrink(2) yields empty (loses 1, exactly required 1) fine. But if slot0 has 5 GREEN, recipe requires 1 GREEN but shrinks 2 → loses 1 extra GREEN. That's a source-confirmed item loss (吞物品) when ingredients are in reversed slot order and the ingredient whose recipe.firstCount=2 is placed in slot corresponding to second. Let's check recipe 1: first SPIRIT_DEW count 2, second GREEN count 1. Reversed: slot0 GREEN 5, slot1 SPIRIT 5. Eject aside. find matches reversed. finishRecipe: slot0.shrink(2) (GREEN loses 2, recipe needs 1 → 1 lost) and slot1.shrink(1) (SPIRIT loses 1, recipe needs 2 → under-consume 1). So net: one item type over-consumed, other under-consumed. Total count: consumption 3 vs required 3 — so total equal, but wrong types. Hmm, so not total loss, but it's an incorrect material consumption, and under-consumption of one type means extra product from fewer resources potentially? Let's compute recipe 2: GREEN(3) + SPIRIT(1) -> LOW_GRADE. Reversed: slot0 SPIRIT 5, slot1 GREEN 5. find: recipe1 (SPIRIT 2 + GREEN 1) matches(first=SPIRIT slot0, second=GREEN slot1) → matches recipe 1! Since SPIRIT_DEW count>=2 and GREEN >=1. So find returns recipe1, output QI_GATHERING. finishRecipe shrink slot0 (SPIRIT) by 2, slot1 (GREEN) by 1 → correct for recipe1. So ambiguity: both recipes match with the same slot contents (SPIRIT 2+, GREEN1+) and recipe1 takes precedence; recipe2 never selected if slot0 has SPIRIT and slot1 has GREEN... Actually recipe2 find: recipe order loop, recipe1 checked first, so any arrangement with SPIRIT>=2 and GREEN>=1 yields recipe1. Recipe2 (GREEN3+SPIRIT1) requires GREEN>=3 and SPIRIT>=1, which also matches recipe1 (SPIRIT>=2)? If SPIRIT count 1 only, recipe1 fails; recipe2 matches if GREEN>=3. So recipe2 only when SPIRIT exactly 1. Fine.

Now the real issue: recipe matching reversed + finishRecipe using wrong counts. For recipe3: VEIN_GUARD(2)+GREEN(1)->MERIDIAN. Reversed: slot0 GREEN 5, slot1 VEIN_GUARD 5. matches? recipe1: SPIRIT required -> no. recipe2: GREEN3 + SPIRIT1 -> no SPIRIT. recipe3: matches(first=GREEN, second=VEIN) false; matches(second=VEIN, first=GREEN) true. finishRecipe shrink slot0 GREEN by 2 (needs 1) and slot1 VEIN by 1 (needs 2). Total 3 vs 3, but wrong. Not total loss but wrong consumption; could be called "材料扣除错位", plus for GREEN, over-consume 1; VEIN under-consume 1. - 炼丹：炉子里已有材料却不想炼时，可以整炉退回——新增 AlchemyFurnaceBlockEntity.ejectInputs（材料与产物都退回，背包满则掉落，炉内工序归零，空炉时明确说明而不假装成功），由 AlchemyFurnaceMenu.clickMenuButton 的服务端按钮入口触发（0=切换火候，1=退料），走原版容器按钮包，客户端与服务端共用同一套菜单校验。

- 符箓：TalismanService.openPicker 把身上每种符分成「现在能引动」与「暂时不行（境界不够／灵力不足）」两栏下发，TalismanScreen 可点可用项，不可用项写明原因并置灰；点选后 TalismanUsePayload 回到服务端 TalismanService.use 重新核对持有、境界、灵力与符纸消耗，失败也按既定规则消耗符纸，不静默无事发生。手持种类不明的符使用右键也会打开该页，不再是原版 fail。

- 拍卖行：新增 AuctionScreen（拍品列表、选中、填价、报价／设上限／结算／翻页），由 AuctionService.openScreen 下发 OpenAuctionPayload（每页 4 条，与界面行高一致，避免第 5 条被按钮压住）；AuctionActionPayload 的 bid/limit/settle/page 全部回到服务端 AuctionService 原有校验（余额、高于当前价、不超过本人上限、到点才结算、获胜者不在线不吞款）。手札 auction_list 动作改为直接开界面。
- 合修：手札新增 joint_cultivate，走 BondService.jointCultivate(player)（默认份额与命令一致 80），仍要求已确认道侣、当前无进行中动作，且只扣本人道龄 30 天。
- 手札新增 talisman_pick、formation_blueprint、joint_cultivate、forge_open 四个动作及其 execution 分支；techniques 动作恢复为真实下发 OpenTechniqueScreenPayload 打开 TechniqueScreen。

- 本命器物：新增 craft/forge/ForgeService + ForgeScreen + OpenForgePayload/ForgeActionPayload。器坊不再是"只能靠命令"，界面列本人器物（刻纹/认主标记、共鸣、磨损、本命方向），可切换器型与品阶后铸器胚，选中器物后可刻纹、认主、祭炼、温养、共鸣、定本命方向；每个动作都调用 ArtifactService 原有服务端校验（材料、境界、认主归属、共鸣阈值、磨损上限），界面只发意图。
- 中英文案补齐（各 3712 键，JSON 解析通过）：炼丹退料/丹方提示、图纸选择页、拍卖界面、符箓选择页与不可用原因、器坊、蛊房、授法、借静室。

content.text:
Important finding: No client code calls `sendButton` / `clickMenuButton`. The docs claim "由界面按钮触发" but grep found no `sendButton` or button in AlchemyFurnaceScreen. So the eject button has no client UI entry point — the server path exists but no caller from the screen. This is a confirmed finding: 退料入口在源码中无客户端触发点 (unreachable in normal gameplay), though clickMenuButton exists. Need to verify grep didn't miss "Button" in Screen — read screen already: no button. So confirmed.

Now the three paths:

1. 退料按钮 (clickMenuButton id 1 → ejectInputs):
   - iterates SLOT_FIRST, SLOT_SECOND, SLOT_OUTPUT; skips fuel (SLOT_FUEL) — fuel not returned. This is intended per docs "材料与产物都退回" but fuel left in furnace. Not a dup/loss, but fuel retained. Worth noting: 退料不退回燃料，燃料留在槽内继续可用；progress=0 but status not reset. Also `mode` untouched.
   - Items: copy, set slot EMPTY, add to inventory; if add fails drop. Note: `player.getInventory().add(copy)` returns boolean and `add` may partially add? In vanilla `Inventory.add(ItemStack)` returns true if fully added; if partially added it... Actually vanilla `Inventory.add` implementation: tries to add to stacks; if stack not empty after, returns false — but items already added partially? Let me recall 1.21.1 Inventory.add(ItemStack): 
```java
public boolean add(ItemStack stack) {
    return this.add(-1, stack);
}
public boolean add(int slot, ItemStack stack) {
    if (stack.isEmpty()) return false;
    ...
    int i = this.getSlotWithRemainingSpace(stack); ...
    ...
}
```
Vanilla Inventory.add actually returns false if stack non-empty remaining, but does it leave partial additions? In 1.21 `Inventory.add` calls `this.add(-1, stack)` which does add items to inventory and leaves remainder in the passed stack (mutates stack). Important nuance: `add` mutates the passed stack, leaving remainder! If it partially adds, returns false, and then `player.drop(copy, false)` drops the *remainder* because copy was mutated. That's actually correct behavior (not duplication). But the `items.set(slot, EMPTY)` before add: if exception... fine.

Wait important: copy = stack.copy(); items.set(slot, EMPTY); player.getInventory().add(copy) — `add` mutates copy leaving remainder, then drops remainder. Good. But there's a subtlety: the original stack in items set to EMPTY without copying back; items.set discards the original stack object, but copy is what's used. Fine.

   Actually potential issue: `player.getInventory().add(copy)` on server with stack size > max? fine.

   - progress reset to 0, status NOT reset. status remains e.g. 3 (RUNNING) or 4 (READY) until next tick. Next tick recomputes status (recipe null → 0). Since tick runs every tick, within one tick status corrected. But if no tick? Block entity ticks. So transient residual status only; client data updates via addDataSlots syncing. Not a real state residue.
   - mode not reset: intentional heat setting.
   - lastCatchup* not reset: display residue only.
   - `player.inventoryMenu.broadcastChanges()` broadcasts player's own inventory menu, not the furnace menu. Furnace menu slots update normally? Container changes mark setChanged, and menu slots for furnace area get synced via `AbstractContainerMenu.broadcastChanges` which happens in `ServerPlayer.tick`/`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl` periodically (server sends changes every tick via `ServerPlayer.doTick` -> containerMenu.broadcastChanges). So furnace menu sync occurs via server player tick. Since be block entity `setChanged` marks chunk save, and menu slot changes are detected by `AbstractContainerMenu.broadcastChanges` comparing remote slots. Fine.
   
   - Duplication? No.

2. 关闭菜单 (removed → container.stopOpen): BaseContainerBlockEntity/Container stopOpen does nothing but decrement unused counter; no item drop. So items remain in furnace. Screen doc says closing doesn't stop tick. So closing keeps items in furnace, process continues. No loss/dup. But note: if furnace is minecart-like no. OK.

3. 打破丹炉 (onRemove → dropContents → Containers.dropContents(level, pos, this)): drops all 4 slots including fuel. Potential issue: onRemove called on both client and server? `Containers.dropContents` in onRemove without isClientSide guard — vanilla blocks typically guard `if (!level.isClientSide)`. On client, level.getBlockEntity(pos) may exist? Containers.dropContents spawns ItemEntity on client-side — but client side entity spawn might just be ignored/or could create ghost items? In vanilla, `Containers.dropContents` called client-side would call level.addFreshEntity which on client adds entity client-side (ghost) — but commonly vanilla code guards. This is a real potential client-side visual duplication? Not item duplication on server. Need to check Containers.dropContents: it iterates container, sets item empty, and `Block.popResource` → `level.addFreshEntity(new ItemEntity(...))`. On client level this would add client entity. But does client have BlockEntity at that pos at onRemove time? Yes, client also has block entities. So client could spawn ghost item entities that are not server-synced; they'd appear briefly then... The client will receive removal for unknown entity? Item entity exists only client-side; vanilla client tick would tick it; it wouldn't be removed by server (server doesn't know entity id) — client-side entity with id from client's local counter... Actually addFreshEntity assigns entity id via level.getNextEntityId() client-side counter, may conflict. This is a known bug class (ghost items). But also `onRemove` on client passing `level.getBlockEntity(pos)` — during onRemove, the block entity may still be there. This is worth flagging as unverified in-game visual only, not server item duplication. Also dropping twice? onRemove may be called multiple times? Vanilla onRemove called once per removal typically; but also called when block replaced by same block? Condition `!state.is(newState.getBlock())` guards same-block replacement. However if block is replaced by another block (e.g., another furnace?) it drops contents — correct.

More severe potential: `onRemove` is also called on chunk unload? No, onRemove isn't called on chunk unload; `setRemoved` is. Hmm, but in some paths, `onRemove` is invoked when the block is removed due to chunk unloading? No.

Double-drop: `dropContents` uses `Containers.dropContents(level, pos, this)` which clears the container (setItem EMPTY). If onRemove is invoked twice (state change sequence), second call finds empty. But the guard uses `level.getBlockEntity(pos)`. After first onRemove, super.onRemove... the block entity still exists until setRemoved. If onRemove called twice with different newState, contents already emptied → no dup. Good.

But bigger issue: item loss on block break? Standard: dropContents drops all 4 slots; loot table also drops furnace item. No loss.

Wait: check ordering: `onRemove` is called by `Level.setBlock` before? Actually `Level.setBlock` calls `blockState.onRemove(level, pos, newState, flags)` when flag 1? In vanilla `Level.setBlock(pos,state,flags)` -> `setBlock(..., false)` -> if existing block entity and block changed, `state.onRemove(...)`. The block entity still present. So dropContents works.

Potential real defect: `Containers.dropContents` drops items at block center; if block broken, fine.

Another candidate real defect: In ejectInputs, fuel slot not returned — but docs state materials + product. Also progress reset while fuel not consumed further; but if recipe remains and fuel present, next tick restarts consuming a coal (progress 0 branch) — actually ejectInputs empties inputs so recipe null. Fine.

Potential duplication: quickMoveStack for SLOT_OUTPUT moves output to inventory, fine.

Actual duplication/dupe path: The output slot is `mayPlace` false, but `quickMoveStack` for index<4 moves furnace slots into player inventory. For output slot index 3 handled first branch. Hmm index==3 handled. For index 0..2 branch `index < 4` moves to 4..40. Fine.

Real potential issue in ejectInputs with `player.getInventory().add(copy)`: vanilla `Inventory.add(ItemStack)` returns boolean, and in 1.21.1 signature is `public boolean add(ItemStack stack)`. It mutates. Fine.

But: `items.set(slot, ItemStack.EMPTY)` then add copy — if `copy` is a stack of count > maxStackSize? Input stacks can't exceed max stack.

Could there be a duplication in `finishRecipe`? It shrinks ingredients then adds output. Output count might exceed maxStackSize because `canOutput` only checks output.getCount() < max, not `output.getCount() + produced.getCount() <= max`. So output can grow beyond max stack size (e.g., output 1 per craft; with mode 2 produced=2). E.g., output at 63 and produced 2 → 65 > 64. `output.grow` allows count beyond max. That's a real source-confirmed state anomaly (overflow beyond max stack size), causing item stack > max stack; then extracting may split into multiple stacks via slot handling? Vanilla Slot.mayPickup etc. would allow taking whole stack of 65, which when placed splits... Actually a stack > maxStackSize can cause client/server desync but typically items still preserved. It's a source-confirmed invariant violation: canOutput checks count < max rather than count + produced <= max (line 209), and finishRecipe grows without cap (317). This is a candidate defect but not strictly "吞物品/重复返还". Still relevant to "产物最终去向" and item overflow. Should report as source-confirmed logic boundary, not claim dupe.

Another possible duplication: `tickOnce` catch-up loop: in serverTick, before advancing lastSettledWorldMillis, it loops tickOnce up to 36000 ticks... then sets lastSettled = now. If loop breaks early due to !changed (e.g., output blocked), it still sets lastSettled = now — time skipped (not dupe). But if loop doesn't break, each tick may complete recipe. OK.

Wait, delta loop: `int ticks = min(36000, delta/50)`. If delta huge (e.g., 1.8M ms), ticks capped 36000, but lastSettled set to now, discarding remaining time — loss of progress time, not items.

Critical duplication question: does `finishRecipe` get called while output can't accept? canOutput checked at line 165/176 before progress increments, so fine.

Another: progress increments then when >= currentMax finish; but recipe validated with counts at each tick; ingredients shrink; if firstCount consumed... fine.

Potential real bug: `tickOnce` when progress == 0 and fuel present: consumes 1 coal and sets progress=1. If output blocked mid-process, progress resets to 0 (line 177) — fuel already consumed is lost (material loss of fuel, not dup). That's intended-ish "停机销毁燃料"? Worth noting: 中途输出被占（例如产物槽被快速移动塞入不同物品？mayPlace false so can't insert; but mode change to different recipe? swapping inputs changes recipe → progress reset to 0, consumed fuel lost). Fuel consumption loss is source-confirmed but is design "重新起炉消耗燃料". Hmm.

Now the main requested conclusion: 退料按钮入口 — the server handler exists but no client UI calls it. Let me make sure no client code sends button id anywhere else (e.g., AbstractContainerScreen has no button). grep for "Button" in alchemy package and whole src.

Also check if `AlchemyFurnaceScreen` has any button rendering. Already read full file: none.

content.text:
Important: AlchemyFurnaceScreen has no button widget at all. So the eject UI button doesn't exist — clickMenuButton is only reachable via network packet sendButton, but the mod's own screen never calls it. That's a finding: ejectInputs is implemented but not reachable in-game (no client UI trigger). Docs claim it exists. Is there any other place calling clickMenuButton? grep shows only the definition. So the player-facing "退料按钮" is not actually present in AlchemyFurnaceScreen.java (129 lines, no Button). That's important — but does it constitute "吞物品/重复返还/工序残留"? No; it's an unreachable feature. Need to state clearly.

Wait — maybe the screen uses a custom mouse-clicked / key? Let me read screen again — full 129 lines read; no mouseClicked, no buttons. So no eject button. Confirmed.

Now analyze path details.

1. ejectInputs (249-275): iterates slots FIRST, SECOND, OUTPUT (not fuel — intentional? fuel not returned; is that "吞物品"? Materials are returned; fuel left in furnace, not consumed by eject. Not swallowed). copy then set EMPTY, add to inventory else drop. That's no dup: copy then clear, add/drop. Potential subtlety: player.drop when inventory full; fine. progress=0 and setChanged. But status is NOT reset; status stays stale until next tick recomputes. That's "工序状态残留"? progress reset to 0, status may remain e.g. RUNNING(3) until next server tick; tickOnce recomputes each tick, so within next tick status fixed. Not source-level durable residue. However, notable: ejectInputs doesn't reset lastCatchupSeconds/Items — display stale catchup message. Minor.

Also: if only output slot has items and inputs empty, eject returns them; fine.

Key issue: ejectInputs does not return fuel slot; if player wants materials back but fuel is kept — not swallowing, it remains in the furnace. Fine.

2. dropContents (325-329) -> Containers.dropContents(level, pos, this) on onRemove. BaseContainerBlockEntity implements Container (WorldlyContainer? no), so drops all 4 slots including fuel. Then super.onRemove. Standard. Potential double drop: is there also a loot table? read loot table — only drops the block item, no contents; so no duplicate. However: Block.popResource default drops... In vanilla, BaseEntityBlock's playerWillDestroy? Actually onRemove is called on block break with block entity still present; Containers.dropContents drops items; then block entity removed. Standard vanilla behavior (like AbstractFurnaceBlock onRemove does Containers.dropContents when state changes). Fine.

But potential duplicate return: the eject path clears slots; break path drops. No overlap unless menu still open — after break, menu is closed? Server: when furnace removed, container still exists? AbstractContainerMenu.stillValid uses container.stillValid which for BaseContainerBlockEntity checks level.getBlockEntity(worldPosition)==this; after removal, block entity removed -> stillValid false -> clickMenuButton returns false. But timing: can a player click eject after the block entity has been removed but item stacks still referenced? dropContents happens in onRemove and doesn't clear items list; then block entity becomes removed; the menu holds old container reference with items still filled → but ejectInputs checks level != null and stillValid checked in menu. level in BE not nulled on removal? BlockEntity.setRemoved doesn't null level. But menu.stillValid returns false → clickMenuButton returns false. So no dup. Unless serverPlayer still in menu and fires packet before removal... normal.

Real potential duplicate: onRemove called, dropContents drops items but items list not cleared. If onRemove is called twice? Now analyze actual defect candidates:

Is that a bug? It's intentional per javadoc; message says "材料与产物已退回". Not a defect, just fuel remains. Fine.

2. ejectInputs clears slot then adds copy to inventory: `ItemStack copy = stack.copy(); items.set(slot, EMPTY); if (!player.getInventory().add(copy)) player.drop(copy,false);` Standard pattern, no duplication. Note `add` may partially add? Vanilla Inventory.add returns boolean true only if fully added? In vanilla 1.21 Inventory.add(ItemStack) returns boolean; it adds to stacks, and if leftover remains returns false, leaving leftover in the passed stack. Then player.drop(copy) drops remaining copy. But wait — if add partially merged into existing stacks and returns false, copy is mutated to leftover. Actually Inventory.add implementation: `boolean flag = this.add(-1, stack); return flag;`? Let me recall 1.21: `public boolean add(ItemStack stack) { return this.add(-1, stack); }` and `add(int slot, ItemStack stack)` loops... Actually in 1.21 Inventory.add(ItemStack) -> `boolean flag = this.add(-1, stack);`? Hmm. It's a well-known pattern used across the codebase (many files use same pattern), and it's the standard vanilla pattern. But note in 1.21 Inventory.add() returns true only if stack became empty; leftover remains in stack. Since copy is cleared from slot before, dropping copy is correct. However possible subtle: `items.set(slot, ItemStack.EMPTY)` then add(copy) — if add mutates copy partially and returns false, drop(copy) drops leftover. No loss, no dup. Unless Inventory.add returns true while leaving items? Not.

3. ejectInputs: does not reset `status`, `lastCatchupSeconds/Items`, `lastSettledWorldMillis`. progress=0 but status stays e.g. 3 (进行中) until next tick recomputes. Since tickOnce runs every tick, it recalculates status, so status leftover is transient max 1 tick. But `lastCatchupSeconds`/`lastCatchupItems` are not reset — screen displays "上次补算：X 秒，产出 Y 份" persisting after ejection; that's cosmetic stale display of last catchup, arguably intended as historical. Not a state defect for items.

More important: ejectInputs doesn't reset lastSettledWorldMillis. Does that cause issue? serverTick with delta accumulation; no.

4. Race: ejectInputs invoked from clickMenuButton which happens in server packet handling between ticks. Items cleared. Then next tick: recipe null -> progress reset, status 0. Fine.

5. Real dupe candidate: finishRecipe when mode==1 and random<0.3 produces residue only, discarding output — no dupe. When canOutput checks before progress; finishRecipe can overfill output stack? canOutput ensures output.getCount() < maxStackSize before starting, and progress increments per tick, checking canOutput each tick before increment? Look: tickOnce: recipe found; status; then `if (recipe == null || !canOutput(...))` reset progress; else if progress==0 start; else progress++ then if complete finishRecipe. So canOutput is checked each tick; when output count reaches max after finish, next tick canOutput false → progress resets. But within one tick finishRecipe adds produced count possibly >1 (low heat +1, high heat +1) — output could exceed maxStackSize? If output has count max-1 and produced=2, output.grow(2) → max+1, exceeding stack size. canOutput only checks count < max. So output slot stack count can exceed 64 by 1 (e.g. 65). Is that dup? It's not duplicating items; produced item count is legitimately added. But stack over max can cause issues? Items in containers can have over-max counts; NBT persists; when moved to inventory, might clamp? For most herbs/pills max stack 64. Actually a stack of 65 in a container can be a problem: quickMoveStack moveItemStackTo respects max stack size, leaving remainder in output slot; no loss. Not dup/loss, but item-count consistency minor. Only reachable when mode 1/2 (bonus +1). Worth listing as source-observable edge, unverified in-game.

Wait more critical: mode 2 low heat `produced.grow(1)` gives 2 items per operation while consuming same inputs — intended bonus. mode 1 30% residue.

6. The key "吞物品" candidate: break furnace. onRemove calls dropContents using Containers.dropContents(level, pos, this) which drops all items in container (all 4 slots including fuel). Good. But onRemove: `level.getBlockEntity(pos)` — at time onRemove is called, block entity still exists? In vanilla, Block.onRemove is called from Level.setBlock/removeBlock before block entity is removed? Actually Level.setBlock: if block changed, calls `blockState.onRemove(level, pos, newState, movedByPiston)` then removes block entity (`level.removeBlockEntity(pos)`) — order: in Level.setBlock, after setting state, `this.getChunkAt(pos).setBlockState(...)` and then block.onRemove. BlockEntity removal occurs in chunk setBlockState via `onBlockStateChange`? Hmm. In vanilla, Level.setBlock → chunk.setBlockState, which removes block entity if the new block's block entity type differs (`if (blockEntity != null && blockState.hasBlockEntity())...`), then LevelChunk.setBlockState calls `this.removeBlockEntity(pos)`? Let me recall: LevelChunk.setBlockState: `BlockEntity blockEntity = this.getBlockEntity(pos); ... if (blockEntity != null && blockState1.hasBlockEntity()) { ... }` and then `if (blockEntity != null && blockEntity.getType().isValid(blockState1))` ... Actually block.onRemove is called from Level.setBlock after chunk update; but BlockEntity removal occurs in LevelChunk.setBlockState -> `this.removeBlockEntity(pos)` if types differ. So by the time onRemove runs, getBlockEntity(pos) may return null → items never dropped → 吞物品 on break!

But wait: other mods commonly implement `onRemove` with `level.getBlockEntity(pos)` and it works because in 1.21 onRemove is invoked before BE removal? Let me think carefully. Vanilla AbstractFurnaceBlock has `onRemove`? Furnace drops contents via `Containers.dropContents` in... Actually vanilla AbstractFurnaceBlock doesn't override onRemove; it uses `BlockEntity` and items are dropped because `BaseContainerBlockEntity`? Hmm, vanilla chests: ChestBlock doesn't override onRemove either; contents drop because `Level.updateNeighbourForOutputSignal`? Actually vanilla containers drop items via `Block.dropResources`? No — vanilla chests' contents are dropped by `Containers.dropContents` called from ... `ChestBlock.onRemove`? Let me recall: `BaseContainerBlockEntity` has `preRemoveSideEffects(BlockPos, BlockState)` in 1.20.5+/1.21, called by Level when removing block entity, which calls `Containers.dropContents`. Yes! In 1.21, `BlockEntity.preRemoveSideEffects(BlockPos pos, BlockState state)` default; `RandomizableContainerBlockEntity`/`BaseContainerBlockEntity` override it to drop contents. So vanilla would drop automatically. Indeed in 1.21.1 BaseContainerBlockEntity has:
```
@Override
public void preRemoveSideEffects(BlockPos pos, BlockState state) {
    super.preRemoveSideEffects(pos, state);
    if (this instanceof Container container) ... 
}
```
Hmm, actual: `BaseContainerBlockEntity` in 1.21 has `protected abstract NonNullList<ItemStack> getItems();` and there is `public void preRemoveSideEffects(BlockPos pos, BlockState state) { ... }`? I believe RandomizableContainerBlockEntity overrides preRemoveSideEffects to drop loot/contents; BaseContainerBlockEntity maybe not. Let me check actual mappings from a dependency jar if available in gradle caches. But instruction: don't chase entire MC engine; if parent timing not enough evidence, write unverified.

But we can check whether project has Minecraft sources available (build cache). Maybe gradle cache has decompiled sources? Let's look for BaseContainerBlockEntity.java in caches. Also check whether the mod's own code calls dropContents twice. If vanilla BaseContainerBlockEntity preRemoveSideEffects also drops contents, then explicit dropContents in onRemove could duplicate items if both execute and onRemove runs before BE removal. Hmm interesting: duplicates! That's a plausible "重复返还" finding. Need evidence about Minecraft 1.21.1 BaseContainerBlockEntity. But user said don't chase whole engine; we can check if Minecraft sources jar exists locally. Let's look.

Also the "关闭菜单" entry: AlchemyFurnaceMenu.removed → super.removed then container.stopOpen. No ejection on close — so closing menu leaves items in furnace (expected for a machine). No loss. But note container.startOpen/stopOpen with player; no item movement. Closing does not clear. Server side persists.

However, there's a material-in-menu concern: slots use plain Slot with container = BlockEntity. Player can place items; menu buttons; slot output mayPlace false. Closing menu with items on cursor returns to player by vanilla. Fine.

Another candidate: ejectInputs doesn't clear fuel/ doesn't clear status; and importantly does not check whether items match; no dup.

Bigger candidate: ejectInputs iterates and sets slot EMPTY, then `player.getInventory().add(copy)`. If player inventory add returns false, drop. OK.

But: ejectInputs drops items at player position, not "炉边" as doc says; trivial.

Potential dupe: ejectInputs and tick race? Both on server thread; no concurrency.

Potential dup from quickMoveStack output: index == SLOT_OUTPUT → moveItemStackTo(stack, 4,40,true). For output slot, vanilla furnace uses `slot.onQuickCraft`. Looks fine.

Now, the key source-confirmable issue: no client button sends id=1; the retreat feature is unreachable through the menu UI. That's a genuine finding ("退料按钮" entry does not exist in Screen; only server handler). Also clickMenuButton id 0 cycleMode unreachable via modal UI too (but sneak-right-click works).

Let me confirm that AbstractContainerScreen doesn't automatically add a button for menu. Yes obviously not. So "玩家退料按钮" entry: no UI widget. Check AssetCheck maybe checks screen buttons bounds scanning files with "Button.builder" — AlchemyFurnaceScreen has none.

Second confirmed defect candidate: menu's `clickMenuButton` allows id 1 while output slot... fine.

Third: onRemove double drop? Need evidence. Let's search local gradle caches for BaseContainerBlockEntity source or class. Also check whether other blocks in this mod rely on preRemoveSideEffects. SharedCacheBlock uses Containers.dropContents in onRemove while SharedCacheBlockEntity might extend BaseContainerBlockEntity → potential double drop. Let's check SharedCacheBlockEntity.

Also check game tests / LogicCheck for furnace tests: none.

Let's inspect SharedCacheBlockEntity to compare pattern — if it extends BaseContainerBlockEntity and both drop, that suggests mod derives from vanilla behavior unknown. Better: find any vanilla-derived evidence locally. Search gradle caches for "preRemoveSideEffects".

It uses recipe.firstCount on SLOT_FIRST and secondCount on SLOT_SECOND — but find() allows swapped slots! `recipe.matches(second, first)` — if slots are swapped, recipe.first might be in SLOT_SECOND. finishRecipe shrinks SLOT_FIRST by firstCount and SLOT_SECOND by secondCount without checking order. Consider recipe: SPIRIT_DEW_HERB×2 in first, GREEN_VEIN×1 in second. If player puts first=GREEN_VEIN×1, second=SPIRIT_DEW×2 (swapped), find() matches via reversed. block.text:
Key finding: AlchemyFurnaceScreen has NO button at all — no addRenderableWidget. So there is no UI button to trigger clickMenuButton id=1. clickMenuButton is reachable only via vanilla container-button packet; but no client code sends it. That's a "dead entry" — not a dupe/swallow, but evidence of the eject button not wired. Note docs say "退料按钮...都没有启动客户端观察" — but actual source shows no button exists in screen. That's a source-confirmable gap.

Now core item-flow analysis:

1. ejectInputs: iterates slots 0,1,3 (not fuel). Sets slot to EMPTY before adding to inventory. If add fails -> player.drop(copy,false). So no swallow for those three. Note: `copy = stack.copy()` then set EMPTY — fine. Fuel slot is NOT returned by eject (design choice; not a dup). progress=0; status NOT reset. status remains e.g. 3 (running) or 4 (ready). Progress reset to 0 while status stale -> UI could show "进行中" with 0 progress until next tick recomputes status. Next tick: recipe null -> status=0. But ejectInputs doesn't reset status; if the furnace isn't ticking (chunk unloaded), status stays persisted in NBT. So state residue: status not reset, lastCatchupSeconds/items not reset. Is that "工序状态残留"? Source-confirmable: status left stale until next serverTick. Minor.

2. Duplication risk in tickOnce: canOutput checked before progress increment on each tick. finishRecipe shrinks inputs by recipe counts. Question: does it re-check recipe matches? At line 176 checks recipe != null and canOutput. Progress branch: if progress>0, increments and at max calls finishRecipe with recipe from this tick. Recipe is found each tick. If player removes materials mid-progress... Actually progress resets to 0 when recipe==null (line 176-180). So progress can't finish without materials. But what if materials reduced below count while progress>0? find() requires count>=needed, so recipe null -> progress reset to 0. Inputs unchanged, so no swallow, just lost progress (intended?).

Potential dupe: at line 190, finishRecipe called; then progress=0. finishRecipe shrinks first/second by recipe counts. It uses recipe.firstCount on SLOT_FIRST and secondCount on SLOT_SECOND — but find() allows swapped slots! `recipe.matches(second, first)` — if slots are swapped, recipe.first might be in SLOT_SECOND. finishRecipe shrinks SLOT_FIRST by firstCount and SLOT_SECOND by secondCount without checking order. Consider recipe: SPIRIT_DEW_HERB×2 in first, GREEN_VEIN×1 in second. If player puts first=GREEN_VEIN×1, second=SPIRIT_DEW×2 (swapped), find() matches via reversed. Then finishRecipe shrinks first (GREEN_VEIN) by firstCount=2 — but first has only 1! ItemStack.shrink(2) on count 1 -> count 0 (shrink clamps at 0). So it consumes 1 GREEN_VEIN instead of 2, and second SPIRIT_DEW shrinks by secondCount=1 instead of 2. Result: recipe needing 2+1 consumes 1+1, producing output. That is a genuine source-confirmable material duplication/conservation bug: swapped slot order lets you pay less. Wait check counts: Recipe first=SPIRIT_DEW 2, second=GREEN 1. Swapped: slot0=GREEN×1, slot1=SPIRIT_DEW×2. matches(second, first): slotSecond.is(first) => slot1 is SPIRIT_DEW >=2 yes; slotFirst.is(second) => slot0 is GREEN >=1 yes. Then finishRecipe: slot0(GREEN).shrink(2) -> 1 becomes 0 (clamped); slot1(SPIRIT).shrink(1) -> 2 becomes 1. So consumes GREEN×1 + SPIRIT×1 for output, leaving SPIRIT×1. Repeat: slot0 empty now, recipe no longer matches (needs GREEN). So only one discounted craft then stops. Still a real conservation defect (over/under-consumption depending direction). Also reverse case could over-consume: e.g. recipe first=SPIRIT 2 second=GREEN1; normal order consumes 2 spirit +1 green. Swapped with slot0=GREEN×3, slot1=SPIRIT×2: consumes slot0 2 GREEN (recipe.firstCount=2) and slot1 1 SPIRIT → pays 2 green+1 spirit for output that needs 2 spirit+1 green. That's wrong items consumed but counts equal. If player has extra, this is *item substitution* (trading cheap herb). Both are source-confirmable: finishRecipe ignores which slot holds which ingredient while find() accepts swapped order. That's a real defect: wrong-item consumption / net material saving.

Also potential dupe via progress retention: progress is not reset when inputs change? It is reset only if recipe null. If player swaps materials to a different recipe while progress>0, progress carries over and at max finishRecipe uses new recipe — consumes new materials and produces new output; the progress accumulated from previous recipe is reused. Not a dupe but progress carryover. Also mode change mid-progress changes currentMax; if mode switched from 300 to 120 while progress=200, progress increments to 201 >= 120 → finishes instantly. That's speed exploit but fuel consumed 1. "工序状态残留" — progress not reset on recipe change: check line 176: if recipe==null reset. If a *different* recipe is present (e.g. change one herb), progress continues from previous, finishing new recipe with less work. That's a confirmed state-residue: no tracking of which recipe progress belongs to.

3. Block break: onRemove calls furnace.dropContents() -> Containers.dropContents(level, pos, this) which iterates container size 4 and drops individual stacks, and clears? Vanilla Containers.dropContents drops each stack and sets slot to EMPTY? In vanilla, dropContents(Level, BlockPos, Container) iterates getContainerSize, gets item, if !empty, Containers.dropItemStack, then container.setItem(i, ItemStack.EMPTY). I believe it does clear. But no local Minecraft source to confirm — mark unverified. Also onRemove: when block replaced by same block (state.is check) fine. Air replace -> drop contents. Also note: `super.onRemove` is BaseEntityBlock -> Block.onRemove, which may call ... Actually BlockEntity removal handled by level.setBlock? BaseEntityBlock.onRemove... In 1.21.1 Block.onRemove doesn't remove block entity; block entity removal handled by Level.setBlockEntity nulling / onRemove invoked... The state removal also triggers `BlockEntity` removal in `Level.setBlock` -> `onBlockStateChange`/`removeBlockEntity`. Ordering matters: if block entity removed before onRemove, getBlockEntity(pos) returns null and items swallowed. In vanilla Level.setBlock: it captures old block entity? Actually Level.setBlock -> setBlockState, if new block has no block entity, calls `level.removeBlockEntity(pos)`? In 1.21 `Level.setBlock` -> `setBlock(..., )`; `LevelChunk.setBlockState` handles: if block state changed, `onRemove` called (via level.setBlockState -> state.onRemove... ) then if `blockEntity != null && !state.is(newBlock)`... In LevelChunk.setBlockState, the vanilla code: `blockstate.onRemove(this.level, pos, newState, flag)` then if block entity and block changed, `this.removeBlockEntity(pos)`? The order: onRemove first then removeBlockEntity (LevelChunk: if (blockstate.hasBlockEntity()) ...). Actually known vanilla pattern: many BEs drop contents in `onRemove`? Vanilla uses `affectNeighborsAfterRemoval` in 1.21 or `onRemove` on Block; BaseEntityBlock registers... Hmm. In 1.21.1, `Block.onRemove` default implementation calls `state.onRemove`? Let me not guess. This is engine timing — put in unverified per instructions. But note dropContents uses this container; if block entity already removed, `this` still exists as object, level non-null, so dropContents would still work since it doesn't need level.getBlockEntity. Unless items cleared. Fine.

Also: if block broken in creative / any removal -> items drop, and block item itself drops via loot table. No dupe: items dropped once. But if `onRemove` called twice (e.g. piston move? or state change to different block and back)? state.is(newState.getBlock()) guard prevents same-block state changes (facing rotation): rotate doesn't call onRemove? Actually setValue creates new state same block -> guard skips drop, good.

Potential double-drop: `!state.is(newState.getBlock())` — placing another block: drop. Fine.

4. Closing menu: `removed()` calls container.stopOpen(player), no item return. Items stay in furnace when closing — intended (furnace persists). No swallow. But if player closes while progress running, tick continues (documented in screen comment line 11).

5. quickMoveStack: shift-click from furnace input slots (index<4) to player inv 4..40. Shift-click from player inv: if fuel -> fuel slot; else moveItemStackTo 0..2 (both material slots). Note order: fuel check first; else input. Could a valid ingredient also be placed in the wrong slot? not issue. But shift-click output index==3 -> moves out, slot.onQuickCraft. Note the output slot is index 3; `index < 4` branch catches 0..3 but the first branch handles 3. Fine.

One issue: clickMenuButton checks stillValid but not that the player isn't... fine. Also doesn't check distance beyond stillValid (BE stillValid uses default BaseContainerBlockEntity distance check? BaseContainerBlockEntity.stillValid uses Container.stillValidBlockEntity: distance <= 8). server-side fine.

Another: ejectInputs only called with container instanceof AlchemyFurnaceBlockEntity — menu constructed with `this` BE, so fine.

Also there's a subtle bug: ejectInputs sets items via `items.set(slot, EMPTY)` and adds copy. If inventory.add partially adds? `Inventory.add(ItemStack)` returns boolean and either merges fully or returns false without partial change? In vanilla, `Inventory.add` calls add(-1, stack): tries addResource; if fails... Actually `add(ItemStack)` -> `return this.add(-1, stack)`; add returns true and sets stack count to 0 if fully added; if it fails, it may have partially added? Vanilla `Inventory.add(int slot, ItemStack stack)` uses addResource which mutates stacks... Known: `Inventory.add(ItemStack)` on failure leaves the passed stack potentially partially modified? The method: `public boolean add(ItemStack stack) { return this.add(-1, stack); }` and `boolean add(int slot, ItemStack stack)` -> `this.addResource(slot, stack)`; if result empty -> true. addResource may partially fill existing stacks and reduce input stack count. If it returns non-empty, we then `player.drop(copy, false)` — but `copy` has been mutated to the remainder by addResource? The passed stack object `copy` count reduced to remainder; the inventory got the filled part. Dropping copy drops remainder — actually correct, no dupe/no loss IF copy is mutated. If vanilla instead copies internally and leaves `copy` unchanged, then dropping full copy dupes. That's engine behavior — mark unverified. Vanilla 1.21 `Inventory.add(-1, stack)` -> `addResource` mutates given stack. I recall In 1.21 `Inventory.add(ItemStack)` implementation: `public boolean add(ItemStack stack) { return this.add(-1, stack); }` and `public boolean add(int slot, ItemStack stack) { return this.addResource(slot, stack).isEmpty(); }` Hmm and addResource uses stack.split? Let me not assert. Unverified engine behavior. Note the mod repeats this pattern in many places, consistent.

But one thing: `player.drop(copy, false)` where copy is remainder — fine either way if mutated; if not mutated -> dupe. Put unverified.

6. Also ejectInputs doesn't reset status, and doesn't reset lastCatchup*. The status field: after eject, if BE not ticked (chunk unloaded, or tick halts when no delta...), persisted NBT status might be stale (e.g. 3 running) shown on reopen before first tick. But serverTick runs each tick when chunk loaded, so status recomputed on next tick. Source-confirmable that eject doesn't reset status; observable impact depends on tick timing (unverified game behavior).

Wait — more important: `progress = 0` in eject, but does not reset `lastSettledWorldMillis`. tickOnce with caught-up delta loop: after eject, if delta large, loop calls tickOnce which with recipe null returns changed only if status/progress changes; returns false quickly, breaks. Fine.

In low-heat mode produced can be outputCount+1 = 2; output count could be maxStackSize-1 = 63, then grow(2) → 65 > max stack size! canOutput passes when count=63 <64; finish adds 2 -> 65. This is a real source-level conservation/overflow defect (excess counts not loss but invalid stack). Worth flagging. That's an output overflow, not a dupe.

Also blocks breaking: fuel slot drops via Containers (4 slots) so fuel returned on break but not on eject — inconsistency worth noting.
